newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caldera reiterates reform commitment.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caldera reiterates reform commitment.

text.p: Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera pledged Thursday to continue with an economic reform program launched a year ago despite a wave of strikes and protests against his government.

"The second part of the Venezuelan Agenda has got off to a good start. The will to carry out the decisions which were announced has been demonstrated," Caldera told legislators in an annual address to Congress.

Caldera, who used this speech last year to announce an about-turn in policy and the launch of International Monetary Fund supported reforms, spoke for about 45 minutes in a breathless, slurred voice, and read his speech from a prepared text.

"This year inflationary pressure will fall noticeably...This year there will be moderate but firm growth in the gross domestic product," he said. Inflation last year topped 103 percent, but is seen falling to around 35 percent this year, according to official targets.

In a wide-ranging speech in which he made no new announcements, Caldera said his government would be careful not to fall into the trap of wasting windfall oil revenues which flooded state coffers last year.

"We have to keep in mind that this (oil) market is erratic and it would be very serious to make the same mistake of previous years," he said, referring to oil boom years which saw public spending swell to unsustainable levels.
Despite facing a growing number of protests in recent months, Caldera said one of the greatest achievements of his government had been that of maintaining "social peace" in the country.
Caldera, 81, concluded his address saying he was confident of handing over to the next president following elections in December 1998.
Local and international markets have been awash in recent days with rumors of Caldera's allegedly deteriorating health.

Palace officials have denied the rumors and Caldera joked at the end of his speech that he planned to end his term "even though the astrologer won't like it" in reference to a local astrologer who predicted last year that Caldera would not complete 1997.
